clue.text: New victory of prisoner involved in appeal

indicators.note: something involved in another thing is caught up inside it, so one word sits within the other

blocks.note: an appeal is a request
a con is a convict, short for convict

explanation.surface: A detainee's appeal succeeds a second time, a fresh win in the courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victory' with 'prisoner' and 'appeal' suggests a court win, but the definition is a military recapture of territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A reconquest is the winning back of territory, a renewed military triumph over land once held.

clue.text: Maybe guy that goes into Public Relations for real

blocks.note: proper means real or genuine
PR is the usual abbreviation; its letters are the outer ones removed

explanation.surface: Perhaps a man who seriously enters the publicity business.
explanation.walkthrough: This works backwards: the answer placed inside the abbreviation makes the word for real. 'Guy' looks like a man but is a guy rope, the cord that steadies a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a cord holding a tent steady, so a guy is one example of a rope.

clue.text: Bird caught, when very careful

blocks.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
so means very and wary means careful

explanation.surface: A bird was trapped when it was being extremely cautious.
explanation.definitionFit: The cassowary is a large flightless bird of New Guinea and northern Australia.

clue.text: Supernatural force within, transformed now to Sith Lord

transformed means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: F is the physics symbol for force
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Star Wars mystic energy turns a hero into a dark lord, Sith Lords being Star Wars villains.
explanation.walkthrough: F joins the letters of NOW TO SITH LORD and the lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not of this world is otherworldly, beyond the natural realm, which is what supernatural means.

clue.text: I’m not sure Greek character looking embarrassed should be judged

blocks.note: um is a hesitant noise of uncertainty
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
someone looking embarrassed is red in the face

explanation.surface: A hesitant, blushing Greek feels they ought to be assessed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have umpired a match is to have officiated and ruled on play, so to have judged it.

clue.text: Occasionally using such, I get niche expertise

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the odd-numbered letters of these words

explanation.surface: Every so often, a person picks up specialist knowledge this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Science can mean a body of skill or knowledge in a field, as in the science of cooking, hence expertise.

clue.text: Retreating king trapped by huge monsters

indicators.note: something retreating goes backwards, so the royal letters are read from right to left
being trapped means being held inside something else, here the abbreviation for huge

blocks.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
CR stands for Carolus Rex, King Charles

explanation.surface: A monarch flees and is captured by enormous beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is Charles, whose royal cipher stands for Carolus Rex; huge is the outsize label on clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcs are the brutish goblin creatures of Tolkien's fiction, a kind of fantasy monster.

clue.text: Always turned up to take in family-friendly show

to take in means to hold within, so the rating letter goes inside

blocks.note: ever means always
U is the British film certificate for films suitable for all ages

explanation.surface: A performer always arrives to put on an entertainment for all ages.
explanation.walkthrough: EVER reversed is REVE; U goes inside: REV-U-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a light theatrical entertainment of songs and sketches, so a type of show.

clue.text: Far-off eruption shocking for all ears

indicators.note: shocking suggests a jolt that throws things into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A distant explosion makes a dreadful noise that everyone hears.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar flare is a sudden burst of energy on the Sun, an eruption very far from Earth.

clue.text: Appropriate tea partner bizarrely beat them all

blocks.note: to appropriate is to take
the biscuit is the classic companion to a cup of tea

explanation.surface: Stealing the snack that goes with a cuppa was outrageous behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective meaning suitable but is the verb to seize. The phrase is British: to take the biscuit is to be the most outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that takes the biscuit is the most extraordinary or absurd of all, outdoing every rival in strangeness.

clue.text: Vessel harbouring is from east state

indicators.note: read from the east means read from the right-hand end, so the little word runs backwards
a harbour shelters ships inside it, so the vessel holds the other word within

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun for a nation, but it is the verb to assert.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward an idea as fact, the same as to state or assert it.

clue.text: Ancient Amazon offering harm, we heard

indicators.note: what we heard is what was spoken, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: Prime is the subscription service sold by Amazon
evil is harm or wickedness

explanation.surface: An online retailer's product causes damage, according to what we have been told.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'prime evil' matches the British spelling PRIMAEVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Primaeval describes the earliest ages of the world, so it means extremely old or primitive.

clue.text: Fruit and veg included in diet before run

indicators.note: something included in a group is placed among its members, so the vegetable goes inside
before places the meeting word ahead of the running abbreviation in the line

blocks.note: a diet is a formal assembly, like the Diet of Worms
a pea is a vegetable
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Fruit and vegetables form part of a healthy eating plan before going jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' reads as food intake but means a formal assembly, as in the Diet of Worms. The vegetable is slotted in just ahead of the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Conference is a popular variety of pear grown widely in Britain, so it is an example of a fruit.

clue.text: On cue, rains regularly mask land by sea

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the odd-numbered letters of these words
a front is a cover or disguise for something hidden

explanation.surface: Showers arrive right on time to hide the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanfront is the strip of land or property facing the open water, a shoreline or seafront area.

clue.text: Fought using right instead of left and failed

blocks.note: armies that fought clashed
R is the abbreviation for right
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A boxer who swapped from left-handed punches to right-handed ones lost the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The L of CLASHED is replaced by R.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer or business that crashed has broken down or collapsed, which is to have failed.

clue.text: Theatrical cast might display such decent art

indicators.note: to cast metal is to remould it, so the theatre word is reshaped into new words

blocks.note: taken as written
surface padding: these words say the rearranged letters show the answer followed by the next word
taken as written; the clue names the leftover word

explanation.surface: A troupe of actors might put on a show of respectable artistic work.
explanation.walkthrough: THEATRICAL rearranges to ETHICAL ART; take away ART and what remains is the 'such' that describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical conduct is morally sound and principled, the sense of decent as upright and honourable.

clue.text: What’s potentially fatty stuffed in typiCAL ORIFICe?

indicators.note: stuffed in says the letters are packed inside the words that follow, waiting to be pulled out

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, shown in capitals

explanation.surface: A question about what greasy food gets crammed into the usual opening, the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals give the game away; the whole clue also describes the answer, food stuffed into a mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Calorific food is high in calories, so rich and likely to be fattening.

clue.text: Idiots gathering beside pits

indicators.note: gathering means taking something in and holding it, so the fools enclose the other word

blocks.note: asses are fools
by means next to or beside

explanation.surface: Foolish people crowd together next to some holes in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysses are bottomless chasms or deep holes in the earth, so very deep pits.

clue.text: Kind of blue diamonds inspector hid in belt

indicators.note: something hidden in a belt is tucked inside it, so the jewels and the officer go within

blocks.note: a sash is a band worn round the waist
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A police officer concealed gems in a waistband, leaving a sort of blue colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour but means sad here.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddish means somewhat sad, and blue is an informal word for sad or low, so a kind of blue.

clue.text: Bath attached to totally exposed dull part like pipe

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its covering, and totally says both following words lose their outer letters

blocks.note: a tub is a bath
the word with its first and last letters stripped away
the word with its first and last letters stripped away

explanation.surface: A bathtub is fixed to a fully bare, drab section of plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totally' applies the stripping to both 'dull' and 'part', not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubular means shaped like a tube, which is what a pipe is: long, hollow and cylindrical.

clue.text: Left holding support going up for part of service?

indicators.note: holding means having inside, so the side word wraps around the support
in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: A departing player lifts a prop for part of a tennis serve.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT holds TEE to give PO-TEE-RT, which reads upwards as the answer. The service here is the service tree, a European tree, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A service tree is a rowan-like tree, and the treetop is its uppermost part, crown and branches.

clue.text: Permanently resume travelling, clamping article to boot

indicators.note: something travelling is on the move, so the letters of resume move about
a clamp grips something between its jaws, so the moved letters hold the article inside

blocks.note: for good means for ever, permanently
taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to go back on the road for ever, clutching an item of footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To boot' looks like footwear after 'clamping', but it is the definition. RESUME becomes MESURE, then A goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: For good measure means as an extra or in addition, the same idiom as to boot.

clue.text: Review power plant being erected

indicators.note: erected means raised upright, so in a down clue the letters read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for power
an acer is a maple

explanation.surface: A report on a power station under construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory next to 'power', but it is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap is a brief summary going back over the main points, which is a review.

clue.text: Top cryptic devices for creative works

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: codes are ciphers, devices for secret writing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as best but is the beheading verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, so they are literary compositions produced by poets.

clue.text: This magician working with fakir might make fruit cocktails

indicators.note: might make says the letters together could be refashioned into the other phrase

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are set aside

explanation.surface: A conjuror teaming up with an Indian holy man could produce mixed fruit drinks as a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a composite anagram: the answer plus FAKIR has the same letters as FRUIT COCKTAILS, so removing FAKIR from the rearranged phrase leaves the magician.
explanation.definitionFit: An occultist practises magic and the supernatural arts, so is a kind of magician or sorcerer.

clue.text: Nancy’s a fine journalist needing provisions

blocks.note: un is French for a, and Nancy is a city in France
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A woman called Nancy has a good reporter who is short of supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' reads as a woman's name but is the French city, so its 'a' is the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unfed has not been given food, so they are in want of provisions.

clue.text: Cooking device turns and tilts

blocks.note: a spit is a rod for roasting meat

explanation.surface: A rotisserie rotates and leans over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns' fits a spit literally, which is the misdirection: it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tips leans or slopes over to one side, just as something that tilts does.

clue.text: Piano piece noted pianist’s rejecting in seconds

blocks.note: Chopin was a celebrated pianist and composer
taken as written; these letters are thrown out

explanation.walkthrough: CHOPIN'S minus IN leaves CHOPS, followed by TICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopsticks is a simple waltz tune played with two fingers, a well-known piano piece for beginners.
